---
title: "Losses and methods"
---

The loss determines the population for which predictions are calibrated. The method determines the form of the calibration map.

## Choose the population

### Doubly robust loss: `loss="dr"`

Use the doubly robust loss to calibrate predictions for the original study population. Supply the propensity score and the conditional outcome means under each treatment as `propensity`, `mu0`, and `mu1`.

The loss uses inverse-propensity weighting, which can lead to unstable estimates when treatment probabilities are close to `0` or `1`. This is the construction used in [van der Laan et al. (2023)](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/van-der-laan23a.html) and the DR-learner literature; see [Kennedy (2020)](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2004.14497).

### Residualized loss: `loss="r"`

Use the R-loss to calibrate predictions for an overlap-weighted population. Supply the propensity score and the conditional outcome mean given covariates as `propensity` and `outcome_mean`.

The squared treatment residual, `(A - e(W))²`, weights the calibration loss. At the true propensity score, its conditional expectation is `e(W)(1 - e(W))`, so calibration gives more weight to people whose treatment probabilities are closer to one half. This follows the R-learner construction of [Nie and Wager (2021)](https://academic.oup.com/biomet/article/108/2/299/5911092).

This weighting can improve stability under weak overlap, but the calibrated scores describe a different population. Choose this target only if it answers your scientific question.

### Check overlap

Start with `dr` when you want calibration for the original population and overlap is adequate. Use `assess_overlap()` to inspect propensity-score tails, clipping, and effective sample sizes. Its severity labels and loss recommendation use practical screening cutoffs.

When reporting diagnostics for an R-loss fit, use `target_population="overlap"` or `"both"` to include calibration error for the population used in fitting. See [Diagnostics](diagnostics.html#target-populations).

## Choose a calibration method

| Method | Fitted map | When to use it |
|---|---|---|
| `isotonic` | Nondecreasing step function | Default for flexible monotone calibration |
| `monotone_spline` | Smooth nondecreasing spline | When you want a smooth calibration curve |
| `linear` | Intercept and nonnegative slope | When a simple shift and rescaling are adequate |
| `histogram` | Constant within each score bin | For binwise calibration or a diagnostic comparison |

The package implements `isotonic` with a single monotone LightGBM regression tree. It supports observation weights, minimum leaf size through `min_child_samples`, and constant predictions beyond the observed score range. The R implementation uses `lightgbm` through `reticulate`.

`monotone_spline` uses nonnegative derivative coefficients and a smoothness penalty. Pass tuning options through `method_options`.

## Choose standard calibration or cross-calibration

Use [standard calibration](standard-calibration.html) with predictions on a separate calibration sample. Use [cross-calibration](cross-calibration.html) when you have pooled out-of-fold predictions and a matrix of predictions from each fold-specific model.
